title: ERC-8004 trust boundaries and attack surface
caption: Where the threats in section H enter. Mutable HTTPS files, free feedback from fresh addresses, the single upgrade key, unchecked proofOfPayment, a reusable wallet signature inside its window, and validator answers that can be lowered. Status of the upgrade key as read on 2026-10-11.
alt: Flowchart of boundaries. Boundary 1, owner to Identity Registry: wallet-binding signature has no nonce and is reusable for 5 minutes; operators share owner powers. Boundary 2, chain to off-chain file: HTTPS registration files can change without an event; capabilities are not guaranteed. Boundary 3, clients to Reputation Registry: any address can rate; Sybil clusters; proofOfPayment is never checked on-chain. Boundary 4, registry owner to all proxies: one externally owned account can upgrade on Ethereum and Base. Boundary 5, validator to Validation Registry (specified): later responses can lower a pass; requestHash is first come first served. Readers sit outside and must filter.
